context.objective: Document how we carry out Client Data Migration, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Thanks for sharing. Give me a moment to digest the file. Then I’ll follow up with a question.
FA-21 describes scope confirmation before mapping and final Manager sign-off. Does that reflect how client data migrations are carried out today?

Yes, that matches how we do it today. The Manager and I, as the preparer, confirm the scope first, meaning the entities, the historical period, the target system, which is either Entrilia or Allvue, the types of data, the source provider and the output reports we need. The Manager confirms that scope before any mapping starts. At the end the Manager reviews the mapping and the reconciliations and gives the final sign-off. We only treat the migration as complete once the source and target reports fully agree and that sign-off is kept.
What event or request usually starts a migration, and how does it reach you?

It is event-driven, so it only happens when it is needed. A migration starts when a new client is onboarded, when a fund changes administrators, or when historical data has to be migrated into Entrilia or Allvue. What I need in hand before I begin is the client-onboarding or administrator-transition request and a decision on the target system. As for how it reaches me, I don't know of a standard scope form or a fixed channel for that request, so I can't give you one. The process owner would have to confirm that.
What do you check in the source data before treating it as ready for mapping?

Before mapping I check that the general ledger covers the whole period from the fund's start through the migration cutoff date. I compare the general ledger and trial balance periods and totals and note any differences. I look for missing or duplicate rows and files and for required fields that are incomplete, and I check the investor reference, contact and banking data against the agreed scope. If something is wrong I ask the source provider to clarify or correct it. I don't treat incomplete source data as ready unless the Manager approves that decision, and the Manager reviews any significant issues. I don't know the formal rules for accepting source data or whether any tolerance applies. The service-line governance owner would need to confirm that.
Once the source data is ready, how do you map its accounts and fields to the target structure?

First I build the Excel migration reconciliation workbook, with tabs for the general ledger, the trial balance, the client chart of accounts, the general mapping and the investor mapping. I load the preserved source data without touching the unchanged source copy, and I record the source totals and record counts. Then I map each client general-ledger code and category to the target chart-of-accounts code and transcode, and I apply the approved formulas to the historical entries line by line. I also map the investor reference, contact and banking fields to the target structure. If an account has no direct equivalent I flag it, and I only propose a new account code when it is necessary and send that request to the authorized approver. I record the reason for every mapping decision and any exception. The Manager reviews and approves the mapping, and every source code has to be either mapped or recorded as an exception. I don't know who actually has authority to approve a new code. The service-line governance owner would need to confirm that.
How do you check the prepared upload files against the approved mapping before they are imported?

I place the mapped data into each Entrilia or Allvue upload template. Then I check the required fields, formats, dates, positive and negative signs, identifiers and the source totals that are available in the template. The upload totals and record counts have to agree with the approved source files, and I make sure I am using the current target template. I save each version of the upload files and link it to the approved mapping, and I do that check for each batch. I get Manager review where it is required. I don't know of a system-specific validation checklist or who would approve it. The process owner would have to confirm that.
After the Manager’s sign-off, what happens to the migration outputs for the first accounting close?

topics.answer: Client Data Migration is identified as FA-21 in the supplied procedure.
The documented result is historical general ledger, trial balance and investor reference data migrated into Entrilia or Allvue, reconciled against source data and approved.

The preparer says migration is event-driven and occurs as needed for new client onboarding, a change of fund administrator or a need to migrate historical data. Before beginning, the preparer needs the onboarding or transition request and a target-system decision.
The preparer does not know a standard request channel or scope form; the process owner would need to confirm these. The procedure specifies no standard SLA or milestone calendar.

The preparer says the migration is complete only when source and target reports fully agree and the Manager's final sign-off is kept. The Manager reviews the mapping and reconciliations before signing off.
FA-21 lists a completed handoff to the first accounting close among its completion criteria.
Whether the documented first-close handoff is a completion condition in current practice remains to be confirmed.
The procedure identifies the Manager as accountable for final sign-off, but says the organizational title and overall program owner are unconfirmed.

The preparer and Manager confirm entities, historical period, Entrilia or Allvue target, data types, source provider and required output reports. The Manager confirms scope before mapping begins.
Before mapping, the preparer checks GL coverage from fund start to cutoff, compares GL and trial-balance periods and totals, checks for missing or duplicate rows and files and incomplete required fields, and compares investor reference, contact and banking data with scope. Problems go to the source provider for clarification or correction; incomplete data is not treated as ready without Manager approval.
The preparer builds an Excel reconciliation workbook with GL, trial balance, client chart of accounts, general mapping and investor mapping tabs; loads preserved source data without altering the unchanged copy; and records source totals and record counts.
The preparer maps each client GL code and category to a target chart-of-accounts code and transcode, applies approved formulas to historical entries line by line, and maps investor reference, contact and banking fields. The reason for every mapping decision and any exception is recorded.
If an account has no direct equivalent, the preparer flags it and proposes a new code only when necessary, sending the request to the authorized approver. The Manager reviews and approves mapping; every source code must be mapped or recorded as an exception.
The preparer places mapped data into each Entrilia or Allvue upload template, checks fields, formats, dates, signs, identifiers and available source totals, and checks each batch's totals and counts against approved source files. The preparer uses the current target template, saves each upload version linked to approved mapping and obtains Manager review where required. FA-21 then documents an import operator confirming entity, environment and template version before importing; the operator's exact role is unspecified.
FA-21 documents running target GL, trial-balance and scoped investor reports after import, retaining settings and outputs, and comparing target GL and trial balance to source. Investor and required prior-administrator reports are also compared, with differences and causes recorded.
FA-21 documents identifying the cause of each difference, correcting the mapping or upload file in a new controlled version, re-importing using the approved method and rerunning reports and reconciliations until no unexplained difference remains. The safe re-import, restoration and duplicate-removal procedures require system-owner confirmation.

The Manager reviews significant source issues and must approve treating incomplete source data as ready. The preparer asks the source provider for correction or clarification.
The preparer does not know the formal source-data acceptance rules or whether a tolerance applies; the service-line governance owner would need to confirm them.
The Manager reviews and approves the mapping, with each source code mapped or recorded as an exception, and reviews final reconciliations before sign-off.
The preparer does not know who may approve a new account code; the service-line governance owner would need to confirm that authority.
For each upload batch, the preparer checks required fields, formats, dates, signs, identifiers and available source totals; upload totals and record counts must agree with approved source files, using the current target template. Manager review is obtained where required.
The preparer does not know a system-specific validation checklist or who would approve it; the process owner would need to confirm it. The circumstances requiring Manager review of upload files also remain unspecified.

FA-21 says Entrilia and Allvue require different templates and reports; charts of accounts, source quality, history, categories, volume and investor data also vary by migration. Current practice and the practical effect of these differences remain to be explored.
When approved scope includes Allvue CRM firms, investors, contacts and communication choices, FA-21 documents additional separate batches, prerequisite export refreshes, count comparisons and reconciliations. The document says current approval and role confirmation are required.

FA-21 warns that one incorrect mapping or formula can affect the full history or multiple upload batches; wrong templates or mappings can cause rejected, incomplete, duplicated or incorrectly classified records.

The working Excel migration reconciliation workbook contains source totals and record counts and tabs for GL, trial balance, client chart of accounts, general mapping and investor mapping. An unchanged source copy is preserved separately.
FA-21 identifies source files, an intake inventory, upload templates, target reports, import logs, reconciliation and difference records, and Manager sign-off as working or retained artifacts.
The procedure does not specify the approved secure delivery channel, repository path or retention period.
The preparer saves each version of the Entrilia or Allvue upload files and links it to the approved mapping.

FA-21 covers client migration of historical GL, trial balance and investor reference data. It excludes the separate Data Team Allvue-to-Entrilia platform migration, correction of client- or prior-administrator-owned source data, business-process redesign and the first accounting close.

The preparer applies approved formulas to historical entries line by line and records mapping reasons and exceptions. FA-21 describes a transcode as a system code translating a source classification into a target reporting category.
FA-21 says governing laws and executed documents take priority over lower-priority methods, and that system settings, workbook formulas, previous outputs, checklists and memory are not governing rules unless approved by a higher-priority source.
The source and approval of the formulas actually used for a migration, and the authority for new account codes, remain to be established. The preparer identifies the service-line governance owner as the person to confirm new-code authority.
The preparer says each upload batch must use the current target template and its totals and record counts must agree with approved source files.

The preparer needs a client-onboarding or administrator-transition request before starting. FA-21 documents a handoff to the first accounting close after final review.
FA-21 directs platform-wide Allvue-to-Entrilia migration to the separate Data Team program rather than this client-onboarding process.
Uses the output of Client onboarding or administrator transition: Request and target-system decision needed before the preparer begins.
Hands off to Data Team platform migration program: Platform-wide Allvue-to-Entrilia work is routed to the separate program according to FA-21.
The current-practice method and recipient details for the documented first-close handoff remain to be confirmed.

The preparer uses an Excel reconciliation workbook and maps data for the selected Entrilia or Allvue target. FA-21 documents system upload templates and target-system reporting after import.
The preparer puts mapped data into the selected Entrilia or Allvue upload templates and checks each batch before import.
FA-21 says timing depends on history, transaction volume, source quality, chart-of-accounts alignment and classification complexity; it gives no standard milestone calendar.

map.title: Client Data Migration

steps.title: Migration need arises
steps.description: A new client onboarding, administrator change, or need to migrate historical data starts the event-driven work.

steps.title: Confirm migration scope
steps.description: Confirm entities, historical period, target system, data types, source provider and required reports. The Manager confirms scope before mapping begins.

steps.title: Is this platform-wide migration?
steps.description: FA-21 distinguishes client migration from the separate platform-wide Allvue-to-Entrilia program. Current use of this routing has not been confirmed by the participant.

steps.title: Send platform work to Data Team
steps.description: FA-21 directs platform-wide Allvue-to-Entrilia work to the separate Data Team program and requires a scope handoff record.

steps.title: Receive and inventory source files
steps.system: Intake log and approved secure source file location
steps.description: FA-21 says to receive the source package, list files with their entity, period, version and provider, preserve unchanged copies, and record missing or replaced items. The secure channel and location need confirmation.

steps.title: Check source completeness
steps.description: Check ledger coverage from fund start to cutoff, compare ledger and trial-balance periods and totals, note differences, and check missing or duplicate rows and files, required fields, and investor, contact and banking data against scope. The Manager reviews significant issues.

steps.title: Request source clarification or correction
steps.description: When source data is wrong, ask the source provider to clarify or correct it. The participant does not treat incomplete data as ready without Manager approval; FA-21 requires the correction or decision to be recorded.

steps.title: Build reconciliation workbook
steps.description: Create ledger, trial-balance, client chart-of-accounts, general-mapping and investor-mapping tabs. Load preserved data without changing the source copy and record source totals and counts; FA-21 also calls for target account and transcode reference data.

steps.title: Map accounts and investor fields
steps.description: Map each client ledger code and category to the target account code and transcode, apply approved formulas to historical entries line by line, and map investor reference, contact and banking fields. Record reasons and exceptions; flag accounts without a direct equivalent.

steps.title: Request necessary new account code
steps.description: When no direct equivalent exists, the preparer flags it and proposes a new code only if necessary, sending the request to the authorized approver. The identity of that approver is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Obtain classification interpretation
steps.description: For an unclear classification, FA-21 says to obtain and record the client or Manager's interpretation, its reason and supporting source. Affected work continues only after interpretation and approval are recorded.

steps.title: Review and approve mapping
steps.description: The Manager reviews and approves the mapping. Every source code must be mapped or recorded as an exception.

steps.title: Prepare and validate upload files
steps.description: Place mapped data in current target templates; check required fields, formats, dates, signs, identifiers and available source totals for each batch. Save versions linked to approved mapping and obtain Manager review where required.

steps.title: Import validated data
steps.description: FA-21 says to confirm target entity, environment and template version, import data, and retain available logs, error records and batch identifiers. A successful load alone does not prove correctness.

steps.title: Correct and re-import failed batch
steps.system: Entrilia or Allvue and controlled upload files
steps.description: FA-21 directs correction of an import error or failed, duplicate, missing or partly processed records using a controlled version and the safe re-import method. Stop the affected batch until corrected and the new import reconciled; the safe method needs confirmation.

steps.title: Run target-system reports
steps.actor: Junior team member, preparer, or system operator
steps.description: FA-21 says to run ledger, trial-balance and scoped investor-reference reports after import and keep settings, cutoff, entity and output. Reports must cover the source entities and periods.

steps.title: Reconcile target to source
steps.description: FA-21 says to compare target trial balance, ledger, investor-reference data and required reports with source or prior-administrator records, recording each difference and cause. The Manager reviews the work.

steps.title: Correct reconciliation differences
steps.system: Reconciliation workbook, upload files and Entrilia or Allvue
steps.description: FA-21 says to identify each difference's cause, correct mapping or upload files in a new controlled version and re-import using the approved method. Link each correction to the original difference and new result; the Manager reviews judgment decisions.

steps.title: Review and sign off migration
steps.description: The Manager reviews mapping and reconciliations and gives final sign-off. The participant treats migration as complete only when source and target reports fully agree and sign-off is kept.

steps.title: Hand off to accounting close
steps.description: FA-21 says to keep approved migration records and hand the account to the first accounting close. The first accounting close itself is outside this migration process.
